`@lynx-js/rsbuild-plugin` (`pluginLynx`) and the plugins it imports must stay importable in a browser Worker, where a host bundles them with `@rspack/browser` and replaces Node.js built-ins with shims. Keep module evaluation free of Node-only side effects: no `require.resolve` of on-disk files, no worker pools or child processes, and no top-level calls into `node:os`, `node:fs` or `worker_threads`. Static `import`s of Node built-ins are fine; do that work on first use instead. For example, `LynxEncodePlugin.encodePool` is a lazy getter that `require()`s tinypool, because tinypool calls `availableParallelism()` and extends `EventEmitterAsyncResource` at import time, and `new Tinypool()` starts its threads at once. `test/encode-pool-lazy.test.ts` guards this through the `process` `worker` event. Only the web target can build in a browser: a native `.lynx.bundle` needs the `@lynx-js/tasm` addon.

The same applies to `pluginReactLynx` (`@lynx-js/react-rsbuild-plugin`) and its webpack plugins. Expose loader paths as getters that call `require.resolve` when read (`ReactWebpackPlugin.loaders`, `CssExtractRspackPlugin.loader`, `ReactRefreshRspackPlugin.loader`), never as static fields resolved at import time; a browser host maps each loader path to a module through `BrowserRequirePlugin`. `pluginReactLynx`'s own loaders stay at `path.resolve(__dirname, './loaders/...')` without an extension: several tests append `.ts` to that path to run the loader from source. Read JSON with `fs`, not `require()`. Resolve packages of the user's project (such as `@lynx-js/react`) with Rspack's resolver (`rspack.experiments.resolver`), not Node.js `require.resolve`, because in the browser only Rspack and `fs` see the in-memory file system. The ReactLynx loaders import the default `@lynx-js/react/transform` statically so a host bundler includes it, and `@lynx-js/react/transform` resolves to the wasm-only `transform/cjs/browser.cjs` under the `browser` condition, because `cjs/main.cjs` also requires the unpublished napi build.

`@lynx-js/web-core/encode` resolves to `dist/encode_prod` (built by rslib for Node, which loads its wasm through `fs`) by default, and to the unbundled `dist/encode` under the `browser` condition, whose `wasm-bindgen --target bundler` glue a browser bundler loads as async WebAssembly. Keep both entries when changing that export.

To check for regressions, bundle the plugin for `target: 'webworker'` and alias every Node built-in to a proxy that throws when used. Keep `createRequire` itself working, and strip the `node:` prefix with `NormalModuleReplacementPlugin` first, because Rspack does not alias `node:` scheme requests. Then import the plugin, call `pluginLynx()`, and run each plugin's `setup()` in a Worker in headless Chromium.
